purpose: Eight Hyperstream shared-player and camera UI review concepts
shared_prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Redesign the supplied Hyperstream interface references into a high-fidelity iPhone UX concept board. This is a visual design proposal for review.
Create ONE landscape image, approximately 2400 by 1600 pixels, with three equally sized, straight-on portrait iPhone screens on a dark charcoal background. Large legible UI, crisp typography, no perspective distortion. Small editorial heading above phones identifies the variation. Small labels above the three screens read "Now Playing", "Camera", "Recording". Each phone is complete with safe areas and home indicator, not cropped.
Reference image 1 supplies the camera context and composition. Reference image 2 supplies the approved Hyperstream immersive Apple-glass aesthetic, readable strong song typography, and compact player. Use realistic optical glass with softly refracted backgrounds, luminous hairline edges and convincing translucency, dark-mode charcoal and restrained lavender accents. Typography is Inter, generous medium/semibold song titles, never monospaced.
Use identical demo content across screens: song "Coastline", artist "Northline", a square photographic blue coastal road album cover. Playback is underway, with previous/restart, pause, next controls ALWAYS visible even in the smallest player. Include a distinct volume icon and output-route icon. Tempo belongs to the SHARED MUSIC PLAYER and is accessible during recording. Show tempo "0.75×", range "0.50×" to "2.00×", and a "1×" reset when expanded. Fine adjustment supports 0.01 increments through clear plus/minus controls where space permits. Seek/progress and tempo are visually different controls with the tempo labeled "Tempo".
The camera view is a realistic full-body adult dancer in a black tee, gray trousers and sneakers in a warm sunlit studio, informed by the first reference. Keep face and torso readable. Camera top navigation is minimal: back chevron with "Music", a small "Record / Stream" selector with Record selected, and a flip-camera icon. In Camera show an unstarted red circular shutter. In Recording show a red "00:18" recording timer and a clearly separate red stop-square button. Music pause and camera stop must have unmistakably different shapes/colors and touch targets. Playback controls remain interactive in both camera states.
Prefer photographic camera content and finished native-looking app UI over wireframes. The concept must be practically implementable in Flutter with native capture. No decorative badges, paragraphs, feature marketing, developer text, arrows through the content, duplicate music players, duplicated transport, waveform decorations, or illegible tiny labels. Only the phone screens and concise concept heading/labels.

variations.title: Persistent glass dock
variations.prompt_suffix:
VARIATION SPECIFICATION
Heading "A · Persistent glass dock". The music player's main tempo control is a normal horizontal slider directly below its large transport row. In both camera screens, a single rounded translucent two-row dock floats across the bottom safe area, overlaying the live picture. Top row has thumbnail, short title, previous, pause, next. Lower row has clearly labeled Tempo slider, 0.75× value and small 1× reset, plus a volume icon at the right. Tempo is ALWAYS visible with no drawer or menu. Thin seek progress runs across the dock's top edge. Place the camera shutter or red stop button centered just above the dock, with clear separation. The dock occupies only about the bottom 18% of the screen. All three screens make the shared control design obvious. Recording screen can show the volume icon expanded into a small vertical iOS-style glass pill at the right, keeping tempo visible.

variations.title: Pull-up player drawer
variations.prompt_suffix:
VARIATION SPECIFICATION
Heading "B · Pull-up player drawer". Main Now Playing includes a dedicated horizontal Tempo control underneath transport. Camera screen shows a low compact glass bottom bar containing cover, track, previous/pause/next and an obvious lavender "0.75×" pill with a tiny up-chevron. A small centered grab handle makes the bar draggable. Recording screen shows that bar pulled upward into a rounded 32%-height bottom sheet overlaying the camera. The sheet has track info, transport, a thin seek line, and large labeled Tempo slider with minus, plus, 0.75×, reset 1×, and discrete volume/output controls. Keep the camera stop button above the sheet within the visible preview. No large album art inside the drawer. The primary UX distinction is compact-by-default and drag-up access to shared music controls.

variations.title: Vertical tempo control
variations.prompt_suffix:
VARIATION SPECIFICATION
Heading "C · Vertical tempo control". The main player uses a distinct tall translucent vertical Tempo slider on its left edge, labeled 0.75× at its top and Tempo at its bottom, alongside central album art and transport. Volume uses a separate speaker control on the right. Camera screen has an extremely compact glass bottom transport bar with cover, track, previous/pause/next and two separate controls for tempo (0.75× icon) and speaker volume. Recording screen illustrates the tempo control expanded upward from the bar's LEFT edge into a narrow iOS Control Center-style vertical glass slider, occupying a peripheral region so the dancer's central body stays visible. Show 0.75× at top, subtle 0.50/2.00 endpoints, a 1× reset at base. Keep bottom transport always visible. The camera shutter/stop stays centered above the compact bar. Volume is not mistaken for tempo.

variations.title: Tempo presets popover
variations.prompt_suffix:
VARIATION SPECIFICATION
Heading "D · Tempo presets popover". Now Playing puts a rounded Tempo 0.75× pill immediately beside the main transport row, with its small rounded popover open below: a row of five clear presets "0.50", "0.75", "1.00", "1.25", "2.00", 0.75 selected, followed by a short fine-adjust slider with minus/plus. Camera screen has a single slim glass mini-player along the bottom with artwork, song, previous/pause/next and 0.75× pill. Recording screen shows a small anchored rounded glass POPOVER hovering directly above the mini-player, containing the same tempo presets and fine adjustment, without turning into a full-width drawer. Keep a separate red stop button above and slightly left of the popover if needed, safely away from playback controls. This option should feel compact, tap-driven, and easy to operate one-handed. Main player and camera use visibly identical tempo popover design.

variations.title: Precision tempo ruler
variations.prompt_suffix:
The Now Playing screen is a dedicated full-screen music player with a small down-chevron at the top, without a Home/Search tab bar.
VARIATION SPECIFICATION
Heading "E · Precision tempo ruler". Now Playing places a horizontal graduated tempo RULER under the transport buttons, with a fixed lavender center indicator, readable 0.75× value, coarse markings at 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.25, and tiny fine ticks. Show a 1× reset. Camera screen uses a compact glass bottom transport dock with cover, song and previous/pause/next, plus a small "Tempo 0.75×" tab. Recording screen expands ONLY the lower portion of this same dock to expose a horizontal draggable ruler with a fixed center pointer and small minus/plus precision buttons. It is a thumb-friendly scrub wheel, not a conventional linear track or decorative waveform. Maintain a distinct thin song-progress line above the metadata. The camera stop is centered just above the dock. The recording view keeps about 75% of the picture unobstructed. Give the ruler clean readable large ticks with restrained details.

variations.title: Two floating bars
variations.prompt_suffix:
The Now Playing screen is a dedicated full-screen music player with a small down-chevron at the top, without a Home/Search tab bar.
VARIATION SPECIFICATION
Heading "F · Two floating bars". Now Playing has a slim glass tempo shelf below the transport, with Tempo, minus, 0.75×, plus, and a short continuous slider plus 1× reset. Camera screen has ONE slim rounded bottom now-playing pill containing cover, short song, previous/pause/next; a small tempo chip 0.75× is attached to its top-right edge. Recording screen shows a SECOND independent narrow glass shelf floating above the music bar, with generous visible camera space separating the layers. This shelf contains only tempo slider, minus/plus, 0.75× and reset. It opens with a tap on the tempo chip and can collapse with a chevron. The two music surfaces are narrow horizontal islands with transparent gaps, never a large solid sheet. Camera stop button is visibly separate, centered above both shelves. Volume/output icons stay in the compact bottom bar.

variations.title: Full player drawer
variations.prompt_suffix:
The Now Playing screen is a dedicated full-screen music player with a small down-chevron at the top, without a Home/Search tab bar.
VARIATION SPECIFICATION
Heading "G · Full player drawer". The left Now Playing screen has album art, song, transport, seek, and clearly visible Tempo slider integrated into the main player, plus queue/volume/output. Camera screen has a compact bottom glass now-playing bar with thumbnail, title, previous/pause/next and a prominent small upward chevron. Recording screen shows that bar expanded into the ACTUAL MAIN PLAYER as a 48%-height translucent bottom drawer, with medium album art at upper left, song alongside it, full transport, seek, Tempo slider 0.75×, 1× reset, and volume/output/queue controls. This should look like the same main player rearranged compactly, not camera settings. The live camera remains visible above the drawer with the dancer's head and shoulders and red timer. A distinct red stop control is anchored above the drawer. The drawer's large top handle makes collapse obvious. Prioritize complete music control access during recording.

variations.title: Adaptive camera frame
variations.prompt_suffix:
The Now Playing screen is a dedicated full-screen music player with a small down-chevron at the top, without a Home/Search tab bar.
VARIATION SPECIFICATION
Heading "H · Adaptive camera frame". Main Now Playing uses a clean complete player with horizontal tempo slider below transport. Camera screen shows edge-to-edge camera with a thin bottom glass mini-player and clearly labeled Tempo 0.75× chip, previous/pause/next always present. Recording screen shows a different spatial solution: expanding the SHARED PLAYER resizes the camera preview to fit fully ABOVE a rounded bottom control tray. The full-body dancer including shoes stays visible inside a smaller portrait camera frame, letterboxed tastefully within the top 65% of the screen. The lower 30% contains translucent glass music controls, track title/art thumbnail, previous/pause/next, seek, Tempo slider, 0.75×, 1× reset and volume/output. A discrete red stop button sits at the bottom edge of the camera frame above the player, separate from music controls. The controls occupy their own space without covering the dancer. Clearly show that collapsing the tray restores the immersive camera view. No desktop or tablet mockup.
